html:
A spirit made by fermenting and distilling sugarcane molasses or juice. It was first made on the sugar plantations of the Caribbean in the 1600s, likely by enslaved people. Barbados is often named as its first home.

Molasses, the sticky leftover from making sugar, had been a waste product. Distilled, it turned into a strong, cheap drink, and a new source of profit for planters. Rum became part of the trade of the Atlantic:

  • New England distillers bought Caribbean molasses and made rum.
  • Rum was traded on the coast of West Africa for enslaved people, who were shipped to the sugar islands in the Atlantic slave trade.
  • The British Royal Navy gave sailors a daily ration of rum from 1655, a custom that lasted until 1970.

British taxes on molasses, under the Molasses Act of 1733 and the Sugar Act of 1764, angered American colonists and fed the road to the American Revolution.
